newsitem.title: ITALY: TENNIS-PIERCE DETHRONES MARTINEZ FOR ITALIAN TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PIERCE DETHRONES MARTINEZ FOR ITALIAN TITLE.

text.p: France's Mary Pierce won her first Italian Open women's singles crown on Sunday to end the record run of four consecutive titles at the Foro Italico by Spain's Conchita Martinez.

The third-seeded Spaniard, who was undefeated on the Rome clay courts since the 1991 semifinals -- she did not compete in 1992 -- and who had not dropped a set on the way to the final, lost to the 10th seed 6-4 6-0.
However the 1994 Wimbledon champion, ranked sixth in the world and appearing in her first final of the year, said later she had been suffering from an old neck injury.

Martinez, hitherto beaten only by retired Argentine Gabriela Sabatini and Martina Navratilova in Rome, had problems with glare from objects glinting in the crowd as she served in the fourth game of the first set.
At 15-40, she walked to the net and demanded action.
Court officials scrambled to find the culprit in the crowd but it took repeated efforts before a spectator's glitzy handbag was pinpointed.
When play resumed, the Spaniard pulled back to deuce, saved another break point and clinched the game.

But the difficulties became more physical in the following game when Martinez broke Pierce and then needed a three-minute injury break, with the WTA doctor massaging her neck and shoulder as Pierce sat with her head under a towel.
"I had a problem with my neck," said Martinez.
"It all happened in the fourth game...Pierce played well but I tell you that from 2-2 I could not do anything."
"I felt I could not really do much to hurt her today."
She said that looking to the right and upwards was painful but she had not considered withdrawing because she still had a doubles final that she was determined to play.
Pierce broke straight back to 3-3, held serve and broke again to 5-3. Martinez narrowed to 5-4 but could not hold her serve and a return to the net gave Pierce the set.
It was one-way traffic in the second set, with Martinez tossing her racket aside and selecting another before Pierce took a break to 2-0 in the second game of the set.
Serving to stay in the match with the score 0-40, Martinez lost to a fierce backhand return and was dethroned after just 80 minutes on court.

"Yes and no," replied Pierce, winner of the 1995 Australian Open and losing finalist at this year's tournament, when asked whether the match had been all too easy against an opponent who beat her in the 1995 Italian semifinal.

"I know what to expect from Conchita. She's a good player...but it was easier than I expected as she got a little bit hurt. But that can be hard too because then you have to stay concentrated and focused and not let her get back.
"It was kind of weird," she said.

Pierce, currently ranked 15th but sure to move up at least one place now, has been helped by Martina Navratilova's old coach Craig Kardon since February and said his experience and advice had made a world of difference to her game.

"He's brought a lot...It's hard to explain, there are no secrets," she said. "The main thing with Craig that I haven't felt up to now with any other coach is that he understands and is always there to talk about it."
"He has a lot of experience.
"Working with Martina for so many years he knows what its like at the top and how to handle all situations, which is something that is comforting I guess."
